svg.text: Node stacking — exploded view (3×10 field), the four builds, and the two bus cable variants
Exploded node (side view along the pin field)
every pin is one net through the whole stack (plated holes only)
front row A = v2 row; row B = bus side (address, I²C, STOP);
the master reads row B and drives CSB, SDA_L/SCL_L, STOP_OUT
boards are soldered, not plugged; the electrode plate is not on the field
stack order is fixed: bus board · master · HMI boards · interface
Four ways to build a node
mono: CTRL drives CSB itself, top pads empty · chain: master decodes A0…A4 · head: STOP_IN unused
legacy: a v2 single-row board uses row A cols 2–9 only (no local I²C, no AUX → the master polls it)
yellow bar = bus cable (18-way, v2 pinout, FPC or ribbon)
Chain along the bracelet — two cable variants, same protocol
FPC: IN/OUT connectors on the bus board, short FFC between nodes
IDC: one continuous ribbon, one connector crimped per node
neighbour STOP link, off the ribbon
shared lines (A0…A4, SPI, I²C, AUX, AREF, power) run the whole chain; STOP is regenerated by every master.
a ribbon cannot break STOP between nodes, so the IDC variant carries it through a 2-pin neighbour link.
